# Bootstrap Interest Website — 100 Points

**Goal:** Build a responsive, school-appropriate website about a hobby, sport, career, place, or other approved interest using Bootstrap 5.3.8 and your own CSS.

**Directions:** Start from the teacher project. Fork your own copy. Keep `css/bootstrap.min.css` and `js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js` in the project. **Do not edit Bootstrap's framework CSS.** Write your own styles in `css/style.css`.

## Requirements and rubric
| Requirement | Points |
|---|---:|
| Bootstrap linked correctly from the local project and visible in preview | 10 |
| Responsive layout using `.container`, `.row`, and breakpoint-based `.col-*` classes | 20 |
| Navigation with links to at least three working sections | 10 |
| Three Bootstrap cards, each with an appropriate image, heading, and description | 15 |
| Bootstrap buttons, colors, text, and spacing utilities used meaningfully | 10 |
| At least five meaningful custom CSS rules in `css/style.css` | 10 |
| Semantic HTML, useful `alt` text, source/image credits, and code comments | 10 |
| Test at desktop and narrow/mobile widths; document three tests and fixes | 10 |
| Submit working project link and short reflection | 5 |
| **Total** | **100** |

## Required project content
- Replace the starter title, introduction, all three card headings and descriptions, and placeholder images.
- Include three functioning internal navigation links.
- Use school-appropriate content and cite borrowed facts and images. If using outside images, upload them into `assets/` rather than linking to a blocked image host.
- Customize Bootstrap components without breaking the responsive layout.
- Use at least five *meaningful* CSS rules; don't count unused selectors or repeated declarations.

## Test log (include in submission)
1. What did you test? What worked? What did you fix?
2. What did you test at a narrow/mobile width? What worked? What did you fix?
3. What did you test after your final changes? What worked? What did you fix?

## Reflection
In 3–5 sentences, explain which Bootstrap classes helped you most, how your website responds to screen size, and one improvement you would make next.

## Submit in Google Classroom
- Your working StackBlitz project link (check that your teacher can view it).
- Your three test-log entries and reflection.
- A downloaded/exported copy of your project files if your teacher requires one.

**Do not submit only a screenshot.** Your teacher needs to inspect the code and responsive behavior.
